correctness_topical.explantion: Both responses avoid factual errors, but response a only omits a single relevant detail (the perception that men are judged as rapists or "creepy"), whereas response b omits that same point plus several other relevant perspectives from the sources and also includes an unrelated bullet about broader societal fears. coherence_logical.explantion: Response b contains an internal contradiction (it claims many men support feminism while also saying men cannot voice their preferences because they are silenced), which is the highest‑severity flaw under the hierarchy. Response a, although suffering from structural and flow problems and some redundancy, has no reported internal contradiction. Since a fatal logical inconsistency outweighs the less severe structural and flow issues present in both answers, response a is judged to have better logical coherence.

coherence_stylistic.explantion: Both responses suffer from severe Tone Clash and Complexity Mismatch, which are equally damaging. However, Response a also contains a Perspective Shift, a lower‑severity inconsistency not present in Response b. Since the high‑severity flaws are tied, the additional minor error gives Response b the stylistic advantage.

coverage_broad.explantion: Both Response a and Response b suffer from the same high‑severity shortcomings for broad coverage: they each exhibit Narrow Focus / Tunnel Vision, Missing Major Aspects (no definition of feminism, no empirical data, no discussion of broader male experiences or coping strategies), Lack of Context, and Superficial Listing. consistency_internal.explantion: Both Response a and Response b exhibit the same high‑severity internal consistency failures: each conflates distinct viewpoints (Blurred Viewpoints / Conflation) and presents contradictory statements without reconciliation (Unresolved Conflict).
